contract: MSVC Win32, 8-bit byte, 32-bit pointer/int/unsigned count, little-endian unsigned WORD16 code units. No Unicode scalar/surrogate/normalization/case/locale/collation semantics.

Count zero accepts any/null pointers and returns zero without payload reads. Positive count requires only actually reached determinate stable readable WORD accesses wholly inside genuine live allocations, including both final rereads. No unused full-count extent is required at early stop.

Reached raw-pointer advances by two are nonwrapping and remain within or one past the same actual allocation; never dereference one-past. Unaligned byte-region addresses, stable identical and overlapping read-only aliases are allowed. No typed wchar/uint16 ownership, padding, initial alignment or arbitrary signed count cap.
After positive entry decrement unsigned local remaining before preliminary reads. A zero residual jumps directly to the final pair, so count one has no preliminary reads.

For nonzero residual read preliminary LHS WORD. LHS zero skips preliminary RHS. Otherwise read preliminary RHS WORD for equality. Mismatch reaches the final pair. Only equal nonzero values advance both actual pointers by two and repeat.

Every positive exit freshly reads final LHS WORD then final RHS WORD, even after preliminary zero or mismatch. Return widened unsigned16 LHS minus widened unsigned16 RHS in signed32, exact range [-65535,65535], without normalized sign or signed16 arithmetic.

Original writes its by-value count home with DEC DWORD PTR [EBP+0x10]. New ordinary unsigned local count is allowed, excluding Original mutable argument-home/stack alias protocols and their writes/fault behavior. No fake argument-block identity or Source parameter binding is introduced.

No SDK wcsncmp/memcpy/search, byte-only substitute, copy, provider, fallback, validation, global/TLS or Original caller binding. Faults, invalid reached reads, wrapping advances, mutation, indeterminate bytes, concurrency, MMIO/volatile protocols and lifetime changes are outside the ordinary domain.
